name: agency-partners
label: Agency & SI Partners
description: Targets decision-makers at NetSuite Alliance Partners, Oracle NetSuite SIs, and ERP consulting firms that do commerce integrations. AOTT's Shopify capability fills the gap these agencies have when their enterprise clients need NetSuite ↔ Shopify storefronts connected. Pure Shopify agencies with no ERP context are out of scope.
_note: AOTT's value is staff augmentation for NetSuite SIs and ERP agencies: their clients run NetSuite ERP and need Shopify (or other commerce) integrations. AOTT supplies the Shopify dev capacity the SI lacks. Target: CEOs, founders, and practice leads at NetSuite Alliance Partners, Oracle consulting firms, and ERP integration shops — not pure Shopify or DTC agencies.
_company_type_signals_note: NetSuite/Oracle/ERP signals are the required primary signals. A company with only 'Shopify Agency' or 'Shopify Partner' in its name — and no ERP/NetSuite context — does NOT qualify. Shopify/Magento signals are acceptable only when paired with at least one ERP primary signal.
_target_industries_note: LinkedIn industry field alone is not sufficient — must be combined with platform-specific domain signals. Focus on companies in IT consulting and ERP/commerce implementation space.
_retail_brand_guidance: A lead at a retail/DTC/consumer brand (not an agency or SI) qualifies as warm or above ONLY when their company is a confirmed Shopify or NetSuite/SuiteCommerce user. The platform signal must be strong and current — it must appear in their current role description, company About section, or company name with clear specificity (e.g. 'Built our Shopify Plus store', 'our store runs SuiteCommerce', 'Shopify Plus merchant'). A vague career mention like 'has experience with Shopify' or a past role at a Shopify company does NOT count. Any title is eligible (VP Ecommerce, VP Marketing, CTO, CEO, Director) — the platform confirmation alone gates warm/hot classification. Without it, classify as cold regardless of seniority.
_excluded_employers_note: AOTT sells staff augmentation TO the partner ecosystem, never to the platform vendors themselves. Anyone whose CURRENT employer is a platform vendor is not a lead: they have internal delivery orgs and do not buy external agency capacity. Detect from the headline when company fields are null: 'at Oracle', '@ Shopify', 'at NetSuite', 'Oracle Consulting', 'Oracle Cloud Applications', 'Partnerships at Shopify'. Watch for Oracle-internal titles — 'Consulting Practice Director', 'Consulting Project Director', 'Head of Consulting Services' with Oracle context (or no partner-company context at all) are vendor employees, not partner-agency staff. Classify excluded-employer leads as cold and cap score at 25 regardless of seniority — this exclusion overrides company_type_signals and seniority_signals. Do not drop them from output; the operator can still manually approve a rare vendor-side contact from the cold tier. Two adjacent exclusions, also cold: (a) mega-SIs with in-house delivery at scale (Accenture, Deloitte, Capgemini, IBM, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Cognizant, Coforge) — cap at 40; (b) in-house IT/ERP/digital-transformation leaders at end-user enterprises or unrelated software vendors (banks, insurers, Unit4, BlackLine, etc.) — cap at 30. The buyer must work at an agency, SI, or consultancy whose BUSINESS is delivering NetSuite/Shopify/commerce projects for clients, sized boutique-to-mid-market like the reference_companies.
_excluded_companies_note: Operator feedback 2026-06-09 (SuiteDB), 2026-07-27 (Seibert Consulting Group), 2026-08-06 (AnagramDev), and 2026-08-06 (FullClarity — no fit for AOTT despite being a genuine NetSuite partner): absolutely no interest in engaging with these agencies under any circumstances — never surface anyone from these firms in any tier, in any criteria. Unlike excluded_employers (surfaced cold), these are dropped entirely at Step 2 — skip the result AND write it to seen.json so it never resurfaces. Detect from headline naming the firm; Seibert Consulting Group's staff may abbreviate as 'SCG' in headlines (e.g. 'at SCG') — treat that alongside any Seibert/NetSuite/Shopify Plus context as the same exclusion. Operator feedback 2026-08-12: N2Lab is now an active AOTT client relationship — exclude from all criteria and never surface as a new lead, regardless of fit.
_search_terms_note: QUERY-BUILDING RULE for Step 2: never pair a bare platform name with a role. 'Oracle consulting' matches Oracle's own Consulting org, and 'Shopify Plus' + 'Director of Partnerships' matches Shopify's own partnerships team. Every query must include a partner/agency/implementation/reseller qualifier alongside the platform name (e.g. 'NetSuite alliance partner', 'Shopify Plus agency') so results skew toward people whose employer partners with the platform rather than the vendor's own staff.
